title: Planck Window onto Parallel Universes
content: Where could a parallel universe show itself in our sky, and how bright must its mark be? We measure this window on the full Planck 2018 sky. A bubble-collision disc brighter than \(153\text{--}211~\mu\mathrm{K}\), or a cosmic texture brighter than \(244\text{--}383~\mu\mathrm{K}\), would already be seen, and none is. The Cold Spot lies just inside the window, \(13\) per cent below the detection edge, where a collision disc fits it at two sigma. Polarisation maps can test it.
